pack.title: Line-cutters
pack.description: The sidle-in ahead of you. Loud enough for the line, calm enough for you.

scenarios.setting: Coffee line, morning rush. Someone slides in ahead of you.
scenarios.jab: Oh — I didn't see you there.

replies.line: Easy to miss. The end is back there.
replies.why: It accepts the excuse and points at the fix, giving them a graceful exit.
replies.delivery: Use a small gesture rather than crowding them; let staff handle a disputed rule.

replies.why: Three words, one gesture — the whole line silently agrees with you.
replies.delivery: Use a small gesture rather than crowding them; let staff handle a disputed rule.

replies.line: No worries — we're all back here together.
replies.why: It points out where the line continues while allowing for an honest mistake.
replies.delivery: Use a small gesture rather than crowding them; let staff handle a disputed rule.

replies.line: Invisibility is my curse. End of the line breaks the spell.
replies.why: It uses humor about being missed while indicating the end of the line.
replies.delivery: Use a small gesture rather than crowding them; let staff handle a disputed rule.

trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Point out a queue position politely.

followUp.jab: I was only gone a minute.
followUp.line: Let's ask staff how returning to the line works.
followUp.why: It handles an ambiguous claim through the queue's actual process.
followUp.delivery: Use a small gesture rather than crowding them; let staff handle a disputed rule.

scenarios.setting: Airport security. A traveler wedges in with the rolling bag.
scenarios.jab: My flight's boarding. You don't mind, right?

replies.line: Ask the whole line. If they agree, go ahead.
replies.why: It moves the decision to everyone affected, which is the only fair court.
replies.delivery: Keep a concerned tone but do not physically block the traveler.

replies.line: I mind. Back of the line.
replies.why: It clearly declines the request without guessing why the traveler is late.
replies.delivery: Keep a concerned tone but do not physically block the traveler.

replies.line: That sounds stressful; please ask staff what options are available.
replies.why: It directs the urgent problem to staff without guaranteeing an exception.
replies.delivery: Keep a concerned tone but do not physically block the traveler.

replies.line: The line can't fly faster; let's ask staff for help.
replies.why: A mild joke acknowledges the problem without blaming the traveler.
replies.delivery: Keep a concerned tone but do not physically block the traveler.

scenarios.goal: Handle an urgent queue request fairly.

followUp.jab: I'll miss my flight if I wait.
followUp.line: Please ask the staff what help is available; I can't decide for the whole line.
followUp.why: It directs urgency to staff without spending other people's waiting time.
followUp.delivery: Keep a concerned tone but do not physically block the traveler.

scenarios.setting: A person joins their friend ahead of you in a long queue.
scenarios.jab: I'm with them, so it's fine.
scenarios.goal: Ask for fairness without assuming everyone agrees.

replies.line: We've been waiting. Please check with staff before joining ahead.
replies.why: It requests a fair process without making yourself the sole rule enforcer.
replies.delivery: Keep distance and your voice low; if they escalate, let staff handle it.

replies.line: Please check with staff before joining.
replies.why: It directs the question to someone responsible for the queue.
replies.delivery: Keep distance and your voice low; if they escalate, let staff handle it.

replies.line: I understand you're together; could you ask staff how they handle people joining the line?
replies.why: It acknowledges the relationship while seeking a consistent rule.
replies.delivery: Keep distance and your voice low; if they escalate, let staff handle it.

replies.line: The queue has a plot; let's ask staff about surprise arrivals.
replies.why: The joke keeps the issue about the line's process rather than the person.
replies.delivery: Keep distance and your voice low; if they escalate, let staff handle it.

followUp.line: Let's ask staff to clarify; I don't want to argue about it.
followUp.why: It moves an ambiguous rule question away from a personal confrontation.
followUp.delivery: Keep distance and your voice low; if they escalate, let staff handle it.
